lede: Portfolio capacity planning compares forecasted resource demand with available team capacity to support realistic project decisions. For professionals managing project portfolios, the course develops practical skills to forecast monthly utilization, profile demand by project phase, and resolve conflicts through resource leveling and smoothing. Learners also build skills matrices and capacity dashboards to validate work intake against strategic goals.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who manage project portfolios and must balance team capacity with strategic demand. It is ideal for intermediate-level practitioners with 2-5 years of project experience who need to prevent overallocation and ensure delivery success. By the end of this course, you will be able to build evidence-based capacity models that align resource plans with portfolio strategy and prevent burnout. This course is designed for: PMO Leader:

prerequisites: Participants should have working knowledge of project management fundamentals (e.g., project lifecycle, basic scheduling) and familiarity with at least one PPM tool (e.g., Acuity PPM, Planview, Microsoft Project). No coding or advanced analytics skills are required. Pre-course preparation involves reviewing your organization’s current project portfolio list and resource availability data to apply concepts in real-world scenarios.
